written.myAnswer: Enthalpy (H) is the heat content of a system. Enthalpy change (ΔH) is the difference between the system’s final and initial enthalpy. It is positive when the system absorbs energy and negative when the system releases energy.
Breaking a bond requires energy, which is absorbed by the system; therefore, bond breaking is endothermic.

Conversion of hydrated salt into anhydrous salt — endothermic; conduction of electricity by metals — endothermic; burning of paper — exothermic; dissolving ammonium chloride in water — endothermic; vapourizing liquid nitrogen — endothermic; formation of rain from clouds — exothermic; evaporation of dry ice — endothermic; dissolving sodium carbonate in water — exothermic.

Heat is energy transferred between a system and its surroundings because of a temperature difference. Enthalpy (H) is the heat content of a system. Heat is energy in transfer, whereas enthalpy describes the system’s energy content.
